Five years of continuous absence under Rule 12 ends the service relationship.
Sub-rule 32(2)(c) is deleted.
authority: Authority competent to grant leave; President for cases beyond sub-rule (2)
time_limit: 3 / 6 / 18 / 24 months, according to service and circumstances
cross_refs: Rule 12 (maximum continuous leave); Rule 40(5) (no leave salary); Rule 27(3) and 29(2)(d) (EOL penalty)
traps: 'EOL carries leave salary' — wrong, none. 'Maximum EOL 12 months' — wrong, 24 for study and 18 for the specified diseases. 'Study EOL needs one year's service' — wrong, three. 'EOL only when no other leave is due' — wrong, a written request also works.

title: Leave to probationers and apprentices
chapter_title: Commuted leave, leave not due and EOL
statutory_text:
(1)(a) A probationer shall be entitled to leave under these rules if he had held his post substantively otherwise than on probation.
(b) If, for any reason, it is proposed to terminate the services of a probationer, any leave which may be granted to him shall not extend—
(i) beyond the date on which the probationary period as already sanctioned or extended expires, or
(ii) beyond any earlier date on which his services are terminated by the orders of an authority competent to appoint him.
(2) A person appointed to a post on probation shall be entitled to leave under these rules as a temporary or a permanent Government servant according as his appointment is against a temporary or a permanent post:
Provided that where such person already holds a lien on a permanent post before such appointment, he shall be entitled to leave under these rules as a permanent Government servant.
(3) An apprentice shall be entitled to—
(a) leave, on medical certificate, on leave salary equivalent to half pay for a period not exceeding one month in any year of apprenticeship;
(b) extraordinary leave under Rule 32.
summary: A probationer cannot be carried on leave beyond the probation period, except on EOL. An apprentice gets one month of medical-certificate leave on half pay a year, plus EOL.
hinglish: Probationer ko leave mil sakti hai, lekin probation period ke aage nahi — sirf EOL exception hai. Apprentice ko saal mein ek mahina medical certificate leave half pay par, aur uske upar Rule 32 wali EOL.
conditions: Probationer's leave cannot run beyond the probation period, except EOL.
Apprentice: one month on half pay on medical certificate per year.
exceptions: EOL under Rule 32 remains available beyond the probation period.
authority: Appointing authority / authority competent to grant leave
time_limit: Probation period; apprentice one month a year
cross_refs: Rule 19; Rule 32; Rule 50(5)(i) (study leave needs probation completed)
traps: 'A probationer may take EL beyond probation' — wrong. 'Apprentice gets full pay' — wrong, half pay.

title: Re-employment and counting of past service
chapter_title: Commuted leave, leave not due and EOL
statutory_text: In the case of a person re-employed after retirement, the provisions of these rules shall apply as if he had entered Government service for the first time on the date of his re-employment.
summary: Past service counts for leave wherever it counts for pension; the leave account follows the pension counting rather than a separate test.
hinglish: Re-employed servant ka purana service leave ke liye tab count hota hai jab woh pension ke liye count hota hai — alag se koi test nahi.
conditions: Past service counts for leave where it counts for pension.
exceptions: Where the past service does not count for pension, it does not count for leave either.
authority: Head of Office / Audit Officer
time_limit: At the time of re-employment
traps: 'Re-employment automatically carries forward the whole leave balance' — only where the service counts for pension.

title: Leave preparatory to retirement
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text:
(1) A Government servant may be permitted by the authority competent to grant leave to take leave preparatory to retirement to the extent of earned leave due, not exceeding 300 days together with half pay leave due, subject to the condition that such leave extends up to and includes the date of retirement.
(“240 days substituted with 300 days” vide DOPT Notification No. 13026/1/2002-Estt.(L), dated 15/16.01.2004)
NOTE.— The leave granted as leave preparatory to retirement shall not include extraordinary leave.
(2)(a) Where a Government servant who is on foreign service in or under any Local Authority or a Corporation or Company wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Government or a Body controlled or financed by the Government (hereinafter referred to as the local body) applies for leave preparatory to retirement, the decision to grant or refuse such leave shall be taken by foreign employer with the concurrence of the lending authority under Central Government.
(b) The Government servant on foreign service shall also be allowed to encash earned leave at his credit on the date of retirement in the manner provided in sub-rule (2) of Rule 39.
(c) Deleted. (DOPT Notification No. 14028/6/82-Estt.(L) dated 31.05.1985)
(3) Where a Government servant is on foreign service in or under a local body other than the one mentioned in Clause (a) of sub-rule (2), leave preparatory to retirement shall be admissible to him only when he quits duty under the foreign employer:
Provided that where the Government servant continues in service under such foreign employer, the Government servant shall not be eligible for grant of cash payment in lieu of leave under Rule 39.
summary: LPR is the whole balance taken at the end: EL up to 300 days plus HPL, up to the date of retirement. EOL is expressly outside LPR. Where LPR is cancelled under Rule 13(3)(b), it is encashable under Rule 39(2).
hinglish: LPR matlab retirement se pehle poora balance: EL maximum 300 din + HPL, retirement date tak. EOL ismein nahi aati. LPR cancel ho jaaye (Rule 13(3)(b)) to Rule 39(2) ke under cash milta hai.
conditions: EL due up to 300 days plus HPL due, up to the date of retirement.
Cancelled LPR is encashable under Rule 39(2).
exceptions: EOL is excluded from LPR (NOTE to Rule 38).
Rule 38(2)(c) is deleted; foreign-service LPR needs the lending authority's concurrence.
authority: Appointing authority; lending authority concurrence in foreign service
time_limit: Up to the date of retirement
cross_refs: Rule 13(3)(b); Rule 39(2); Rule 31 (LND not for LPR)
traps: 'LPR can include EOL' — wrong. 'LPR EL limit is 240 days' — wrong, amended to 300 in 2004. 'LND can extend LPR' — wrong.

title: Earned leave encashment with LTC
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text:
(1) A Government servant may be permitted to encash earned leave up to ten days at the time of availing of Leave Travel Concession while in service, subject to the conditions that—
(a) a balance of at least thirty days of earned leave is available to his credit after taking into account the period of encashment as well as leave being availed of:
(b) the total leave so encashed during the entire career does not exceed sixty days in the aggregate;
(2) The cash equivalent for encashment of leave under sub-rule (1) shall be calculated as follows, namely:—
Cash equivalent = [(Pay admissible on the date of availing of the Leave Travel Concession plus Dearness Allowance admissible on that date) ÷ 30] × Number of days of earned leave subject to the maximum of 10 days at one time.
(3) No House Rent Allowance shall be included in the cash equivalent calculated under sub-rule (2);
(4) The period of earned leave encashed shall not be deducted from the quantum of leave that can normally be encashed by the Government servant under Rules 6, 39, 39-A, 39-B, 39-C and 39-D.
(5) If the Government servant fails to avail the Leave Travel Concession within the time prescribed under the Central Civil Services (Leave Travel Concession) Rules, 1988, then he shall be required to refund the entire amount of leave so encashed along with interest at the rate of two per cent above the rate of interest allowed by the Government as applicable to Provident Fund balances and shall also be entitled for credit back of leave so debited for leave encashment.
(DOPT Notification No. 14028/1/2010-Estt.(L), dated 26.08.2011)
summary: LTC encashment: 10 days per occasion, 60 days in the career, and at least 30 days of EL must remain after encashment. If the LTC is not availed, the money comes back with interest at 2% above the PF rate.
hinglish: LTC ke saath EL encash: ek baar mein 10 din, poore career mein 60 din, aur encash ke baad kam se kam 30 din EL bachni chahiye. LTC use nahi kiya to refund + PF rate se 2% zyada interest.
conditions: 10 days per LTC occasion.
60 days in the entire career.
Minimum EL balance of 30 days after encashment.
Refund with interest at 2% above the PF rate if the LTC is not availed.
exceptions: This is separate from retirement encashment and is not deducted from it.
authority: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
time_limit: Per LTC occasion; 60 days per career
traps: '60 per occasion' — wrong, 10. 'Career total 300' — wrong, 60. 'No minimum balance' — wrong, 30 days must remain.

title: Cash in lieu of leave on retirement
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text:
(1) No leave shall be granted to a Government servant beyond—
(a) the date of his retirement, or
(b) the date of his final cessation of duties, or
(c) the date on which he retires by giving notice to Government or he is retired by Government by giving him notice or pay and allowances in lieu of such notice, in accordance with the terms and conditions of his service, or
(d) the date of his resignation from service.
(2)(a) Where a Government servant retires on attaining the normal age prescribed for retirement under the terms and conditions governing his service, the authority competent to grant leave shall, suo motu, issue an order granting cash equivalent of leave salary for both earned leave and half pay leave, if any, at the credit of the Government servant on the date of his retirement subject to a maximum of 300 days;
(b) The cash equivalent of leave salary under Clause (a) shall be calculated as follows and shall be payable in one lumpsum as a one-time settlement,—
(i) Cash equivalent for earned leave = [(Pay admissible on the date of retirement plus Dearness Allowance admissible on that date) ÷ 30] × Number of days of unutilized earned leave at credit subject to the total of earned leave and half pay leave not exceeding 300 days;
(ii) Cash payment in lieu of half pay leave component = [(Half pay leave salary admissible on the date of retirement plus Dearness Allowance admissible on that date) ÷ 30] × Number of days of half pay leave at credit subject to the total of earned leave and half pay leave at credit not exceeding 300 days.
NOTE.— The overall limit for encashment of leave including both earned leave and half pay leave shall not exceed 300 days.
(c) To make up the shortfall in earned leave, no commutation of half pay leave shall be permissible.
(DOPT Notification No. 11012/1/2009-Estt.(L), dated 01.12.2009)
summary: On retirement the authority acts suo motu: EL and HPL are both encashed, together capped at 300 days, on the retirement-date pay plus DA. HPL cannot be commuted to top up an EL shortfall. Nothing is paid on resignation, dismissal or removal — that is Rule 9.
hinglish: Retirement par authority khud order nikaalti hai: EL + HPL dono cash, total 300 din tak, retirement date ke pay + DA par. EL ki kami ko HPL commute karke nahi bhara ja sakta. Resignation/dismissal/removal par kuch nahi milta — woh Rule 9 hai.
conditions: EL and HPL are both encashed, capped at 300 days combined.
Cash equivalent = (Pay + DA) × days ÷ 30.
The order is issued suo motu.
exceptions: No commutation of HPL to fill an EL shortfall.
Payment may be withheld in whole or part where disciplinary proceedings are pending.
Nothing is payable on resignation, dismissal or removal.
authority: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
time_limit: Suo motu on the date of retirement
cross_refs: Rule 9 (lapse); Rule 26 (EL ceiling); Rule 39-A to 39-D (other events)
traps: 'HPL can be commuted to top up EL' — wrong. 'Cash equivalent is at the last basic pay only' — wrong, pay plus DA. 'Resignation earns encashment' — wrong, Rule 9 lapses the balance.

title: Cash equivalent on death in service
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text: 39-A. Where a Government servant dies while in service, the cash equivalent of the leave salary that the deceased would have got had he gone on earned leave, not exceeding leave salary for 300 days (including days for which encashment was allowed along with LTC while in service), shall be paid to his family without any reduction on account of the pension equivalent of death-cum-retirement gratuity. The family is also entitled to dearness allowance.
summary: Death in service: the family gets cash equivalent of up to 300 days, computed as if the servant had gone on earned leave on the day after death. LTC encashment already taken is subtracted from the 300-day ceiling, and there is no DCRG set-off.
hinglish: Death in service: family ko 300 din tak ka cash equivalent, is tarah gino jaise servant death ke agle din EL par gaya ho. Life mein LTC ki encash li thi to woh 300 se ghata do — jaise 40 din LTC liye to 260 din bache. DCRG ke pension equivalent ki koi katauti nahi.
conditions: Ceiling 300 days, including LTC encashment already availed.
No reduction on account of the pension equivalent of DCRG.
Dearness allowance is also payable.
exceptions: LTC encashment taken in service reduces the available ceiling.
authority: Head of Office (payment to the family)
time_limit: Date immediately following death is the calculation date
traps: 'Full 300 days are always paid' — wrong if LTC encashment was taken. 'DCRG is set off' — wrong.

title: Cash equivalent on invalidation
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text:
39-B. (1) A Government servant declared completely and permanently incapacitated for further service may be granted suo motu cash equivalent for both earned leave and half pay leave at credit on the date of invalidation, subject to a maximum of 300 days.
(2) A Government servant not in permanent or quasi-permanent employ shall not be granted cash equivalent of half pay leave on invalidation.
summary: Invalidation on permanent incapacity: EL and HPL both encashed, 300-day cap, suo motu. A non-permanent or non-quasi-permanent servant gets EL only — no HPL.
hinglish: Permanent invalidation par EL + HPL dono, 300 din tak, suo motu. Lekin non-permanent/non-quasi-permanent ko sirf EL — HPL ka cash nahi.
conditions: EL and HPL both encashable, 300 days combined, for permanent and quasi-permanent staff.
The order is issued suo motu.
exceptions: Non-permanent staff: EL only, no HPL cash equivalent.
authority: Head of Office
time_limit: Date of invalidation
traps: 'Invalidation always includes HPL' — wrong for non-permanent staff. 'The servant must apply' — wrong, it is suo motu.

title: Order of payment of cash equivalent
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text: 39-C. Where a Government servant dies before actual receipt of the cash equivalent, payment shall be made in the following order: widow/husband (eldest surviving widow if more than one), eldest surviving son or adopted son, eldest surviving unmarried daughter, eldest surviving widowed daughter, father, mother, eldest surviving married daughter, eldest surviving brother below 18 years, eldest surviving unmarried sister, eldest surviving widowed sister, eldest child of the eldest predeceased son.
summary: The succession ladder for money not yet received: widow or husband, son, unmarried daughter, widowed daughter, father, mother, married daughter, minor brother, unmarried sister, widowed sister, then the eldest child of the eldest predeceased son.
hinglish: Payment priority: widow/husband → son → unmarried daughter → widowed daughter → father → mother → married daughter → 18 se chhota brother → unmarried sister → widowed sister → predeceased son ka eldest child. Note: seniority age se nahi, marriage date se.
conditions: Father ranks after the widowed daughter.
Where there is more than one widow, the eldest surviving widow is senior by date of marriage, not by age.
exceptions: The order applies only where the servant died before actual receipt.
authority: Head of Office
time_limit: At the time of payment
traps: 'Father comes before the unmarried daughter' — wrong. 'Eldest widow means eldest by age' — wrong, by date of marriage.

title: Cash equivalent on permanent absorption in a PSU
chapter_title: Leave preparatory to retirement and encashment
statutory_text: 39-D. A Government servant permitted to be absorbed in a public sector undertaking or autonomous body wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Central Government or a State Government shall be granted suo motu cash equivalent of the earned leave at credit on the date of absorption, subject to a maximum of 300 days.
summary: PSU absorption: earned leave only, up to 300 days, suo motu. HPL is not encashed. The body must be wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Central or a State Government.
hinglish: PSU absorption par sirf EL ka cash — HPL nahi — maximum 300 din, suo motu. PSU Central ya State Government ke wholly/substantially ownership ya control mein honi chahiye, aur servant ne proper channel se apply karke resignation diya ho.
conditions: Earned leave only, up to 300 days, suo motu.
exceptions: HPL is not encashable on this route.
The PSU or autonomous body must be wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Central or a State Government.
authority: Head of Office
time_limit: Date of absorption
traps: '39-D includes HPL' — wrong. 'Any PSU absorption qualifies' — wrong, ownership and proper-channel conditions apply.

title: Leave salary
statutory_text:
40. (1) A Government servant on earned leave shall be paid leave salary equal to the pay drawn immediately before proceeding on earned leave.
(3) Half pay leave and leave not due carry half of the amount under sub-rule (1).
(4) Commuted leave carries full pay, as under sub-rule (1).
(5) No leave salary is admissible during extraordinary leave.
(7)(c) Re-employed servants draw leave salary as provided in the sub-rule.
summary: The master rate card: EL full pay, HPL and LND half pay, commuted leave full pay, EOL nothing. DA follows; HRA applies on the stated conditions.
hinglish: Leave salary ka rate chart: EL = full pay, HPL/LND = half pay, commuted leave = full pay, EOL = zero. DA saath chalta hai; HRA conditions ke saath.
conditions: EL: full pay (the last drawn pay).
HPL and LND: half pay.
Commuted leave: full pay.
EOL: no leave salary.
exceptions: Maternity, paternity, child adoption and the first 365 days of CCL are at full pay under their own rules.
authority: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
time_limit: Paid monthly
cross_refs: Rule 40 read with Rules 43, 43-A, 43-B, 43-C, 49 (departmental leave at 25%)
traps: 'Commuted leave is paid at half pay' — wrong. 'EOL attracts DA' — wrong, nothing is payable.

title: Drawal of leave salary
statutory_text: 41. The leave salary payable under these rules shall be drawn in rupees in India.
summary: Leave salary is drawn in rupees, in India — even where the servant is on leave abroad.
hinglish: Leave salary hamesha INR mein aur India mein draw hogi — chahe servant bahar desh mein leave pe ho.
conditions: Currency: Indian rupees.
Place of drawal: India.
exceptions: The rule does not permit drawal in foreign currency.
authority: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
time_limit: Monthly drawal
traps: 'Leave salary abroad is paid in foreign currency' — wrong. 'It can be drawn at the Mission' — not under this rule.

title: Advance of leave salary
statutory_text: 42. A Government servant, including a Government servant on foreign service, proceeding on leave for a period of not less than thirty days may be allowed an advance in lieu of leave salary up to a month's pay and allowances admissible on that leave salary, subject to deductions on account of income tax, provident fund, house rent, recovery of advances, etc.
summary: Advance of leave salary: leave of at least 30 days, advance up to one month's pay and allowances computed on the leave salary admissible, less statutory deductions.
hinglish: 30 din ya usse zyada leave par advance mil sakta hai — maximum ek mahine ka pay + allowances, leave salary ke hisaab se, minus IT, PF, house rent, purane advance aadi.
conditions: Minimum leave period: 30 days.
Maximum advance: one month's pay and allowances admissible on that leave salary.
Deductions: income tax, PF, house rent, recovery of advances.
exceptions: Leave of 29 days or less attracts no advance.
authority: Head of Office
time_limit: Leave of at least 30 days
traps: 'Advance is available on 15 days' leave' — wrong, 30. 'Advance equals one month of full pay even on HPL' — wrong, it follows the leave salary admissible.

title: Maternity leave
statutory_text:
43. (1) A female Government servant (including an apprentice) with less than two surviving children may be granted maternity leave for a period of 180 days from the date of its commencement.
(2) During such period she shall be paid leave salary equal to the pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave.
(3) Maternity leave not exceeding 45 days may also be granted, irrespective of the number of surviving children, in case of miscarriage including abortion, on production of a medical certificate.
(4)(a) Maternity leave may be combined with leave of any other kind.
(b) Leave of the kind due and admissible, including commuted leave up to 60 days and leave not due, up to a maximum of two years may be granted in continuation of maternity leave.
(5) Maternity leave shall not be debited against the leave account.
summary: Maternity leave: 180 days on full pay for a female servant with fewer than two surviving children; 45 days for miscarriage or abortion, irrespective of the number of children. It is not debited to the leave account, may be combined with any leave, and due leave up to two years may follow it.
hinglish: Maternity leave 180 din full pay par — sirf tab jab do se kam surviving children hon. Miscarriage/abortion par 45 din — bachchon ki ginti ka koi bar. Leave account se debit nahi hoti, kisi bhi leave ke saath combine ho sakti hai, aur uske baad 2 saal tak due leave mil sakti hai.
conditions: Duration: 180 days from the date of commencement.
Eligibility: fewer than two surviving children.
Salary: full pay.
Miscarriage or abortion: up to 45 days, irrespective of surviving children.
May be combined with any other leave.
Due leave up to two years may follow maternity leave (commuted leave up to 60 days, plus LND).
Not debited to the leave account.
exceptions: The 45-day miscarriage leave has no surviving-children condition.
The 180-day leave is not available where two or more children survive.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority or delegated subordinate
time_limit: 180 days; 45 days for miscarriage/abortion
cross_refs: Rule 11 (combination); Rule 43-A (paternity); Rule 43-B (child adoption); Rule 43-C (child care)
traps: 'Maternity leave is 135 days' — wrong, amended to 180. 'Available regardless of children' — wrong. 'Miscarriage is 30 days' — wrong, 45. 'Debited to the leave account' — wrong. 'Continuation limited to one year' — wrong, two.

title: Paternity leave
statutory_text: 43-A. A male Government servant (including an apprentice) with less than two surviving children may be granted paternity leave for a period of 15 days, during the period from 15 days before the expected date of delivery to six months from the date of delivery. The leave shall lapse where it is not availed within that period.
summary: Paternity leave: 15 days for a male servant with fewer than two surviving children, availed within the window from 15 days before delivery to six months after it. The leave lapses if not taken in that window.
hinglish: Paternity leave 15 din — do se kam surviving children. Window: delivery se 15 din pehle se delivery ke 6 mahine tak. Is window mein na li to lapse.
conditions: 15 days.
Eligibility: fewer than two surviving children.
Window: 15 days before the expected date of delivery to six months after delivery.
The leave lapses if not availed within the window.
exceptions: Not a single block requirement — it may be taken in the window.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority or delegated subordinate
time_limit: Window: 15 days before delivery to 6 months after
traps: 'Paternity leave is 30 days' — wrong, 15. 'It can be taken any time' — wrong, the window governs. 'Available with two surviving children' — wrong.

title: Paternity leave on adoption
statutory_text: 43-AA. A male Government servant (including an apprentice) with less than two surviving children may be granted paternity leave for a period of 15 days on the valid adoption of a child below one year of age, within six months of such adoption.
summary: Paternity leave on adoption: 15 days, on a valid adoption of a child below one year, availed within six months of the adoption.
hinglish: Adoption par paternity leave 15 din — adopt kiya bachcha 1 saal se chhota ho, aur adoption ke 6 mahine ke andar li jaaye.
conditions: 15 days.
Child below one year of age.
Valid adoption; within six months of adoption.
Eligibility: fewer than two surviving children.
exceptions: The child's age condition is one year, not the 18 years used for CCL.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
time_limit: Within 6 months of adoption
traps: 'Child may be up to 18 years' — wrong, below one year. 'No time limit to avail' — wrong, six months.

title: Child adoption leave
statutory_text: 43-B. A female Government servant with less than two surviving children may be granted child adoption leave for a period of 180 days from the date of valid adoption of a child below one year of age. The leave shall not be debited against the leave account.
summary: Child adoption leave: 180 days for a female servant with fewer than two surviving children, on a valid adoption of a child below one year. Not debited to the account.
hinglish: Female servant ko child adoption leave 180 din — valid adoption par, bachcha 1 saal se chhota, aur do se kam surviving children. Leave account se debit nahi.
conditions: 180 days.
Female Government servant.
Child below one year; valid adoption.
Not debited against the leave account.
exceptions: Eligibility is fewer than two surviving children.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
time_limit: 180 days from the date of adoption
traps: 'Child adoption leave is for male employees' — wrong, it is for female employees; the male counterpart is 15 days under Rule 43-AA. 'Debited to the account' — wrong.

title: Child care leave
statutory_text:
43-C. (1) Child care leave may be granted to a female Government servant, and to a single male parent, for the care of the two eldest surviving children, up to a total of 730 days in the entire service.
(2) 'Child' means a child below 18 years of age, or a child of any age with a minimum disability of 40%.
(3) Not more than three spells in a calendar year; six spells for a single female parent; not ordinarily during probation; not less than five days at a time; maximum 120 days in a spell.
(4) Leave salary: 100% of pay for the first 365 days and 80% for the next 365 days.
(5) May be combined with any other leave.
(6) Due leave up to one year may be granted in continuation.
(7) Shall not be debited against the leave account.
summary: Child care leave: 730 days in the entire service for the two eldest surviving children, at 100% pay for the first 365 days and 80% for the next 365. Spells: 3 a year normally, 6 for a single female parent, minimum 5 days, maximum 120 days a spell. Available to female servants and single male parents.
hinglish: CCL: poore service mein 730 din, sirf do sabse bade surviving children ke liye. Pay: pehle 365 din 100%, agle 365 din 80%. Spells: aam taur par 3 saal mein, single female parent ke liye 6, ek spell minimum 5 din aur maximum 120 din. Single male parent (unmarried/widower/divorcee) ko bhi milti hai.
conditions: Maximum 730 days in the entire service.
Only the two eldest surviving children.
Child: below 18 years, or any age with at least 40% disability.
Three spells a year; six for a single female parent.
Minimum 5 days a spell; maximum 120 days a spell.
Salary: 100% for the first 365 days, 80% for the next 365.
May be combined with any other leave.
Not debited against the leave account.
exceptions: Not ordinarily admissible during probation except in extreme situations.
Single male parent means unmarried, widower or divorcee.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
time_limit: 730 days in the entire service; 120 days a spell
traps: 'CCL is 365 days' — wrong, 730. 'Any child' — wrong, the two eldest surviving. 'Age limit 12 years' — wrong, 18 (or 40% disability at any age). '100% throughout' — wrong, 80% after 365 days. 'Married male employees' — wrong, only a single male parent. 'Minimum one day' — wrong, five.

title: Work related injury or illness leave (WRIIL)
statutory_text:
44. (1) Full pay and allowances are admissible during the entire period of hospitalisation on account of a work related injury or illness.
(2)(a) For a servant other than a military servant: full pay and allowances for six months after hospitalisation, and half pay for a further twelve months; the half pay period may be commuted to full pay by debiting an equal amount of half pay leave.
(b) CAPF officers: full pay and allowances for six months after hospitalisation and full pay for the next twenty-four months.
(c) CAPF personnel below officer rank: full pay and allowances with no limit on the period.
(3) Where the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 applies, leave salary under this rule is reduced by the compensation payable under that Act.
(4) No earned leave or half pay leave shall be credited during the period of WRIIL.
summary: WRIIL replaced the old special disability leave and hospital leave from 14.12.2018. Full pay during hospitalisation; beyond it, 6 months full pay plus 12 months half pay for civil servants, 6 + 24 months full pay for CAPF officers, and no limit for CAPF below officer rank. No EL or HPL is credited during WRIIL.
hinglish: WRIIL (14.12.2018 se): hospitalisation ke dauran full pay. Uske baad civil servant ko 6 mahine full + 12 mahine half pay (half ko HPL debit karke full banaya ja sakta hai); CAPF officer 6 + 24 mahine full pay; CAPF below officer rank ko koi limit nahi. WRIIL ke dauran EL/HPL credit nahi hoti.
conditions: Hospitalisation: full pay and allowances throughout.
Civil servants: 6 months full pay after hospitalisation, then 12 months half pay, commutable to full pay by debiting HPL.
CAPF officers: 6 months full pay, then 24 months full pay.
CAPF below officer rank: no limit.
No EL or HPL is credited during WRIIL.
exceptions: Leave salary is reduced by Workmen's Compensation Act compensation where that Act applies.
Rules 45 (special disability leave) and 46 (hospital leave) stand omitted.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
time_limit: 6 + 12 months (civil); 6 + 24 (CAPF officers); no limit for CAPF below officer rank
traps: 'WRIIL is half pay throughout' — wrong. 'EL/HPL are credited during WRIIL' — wrong. 'CAPF below officer rank gets half pay after six months' — wrong, no limit at full pay. 'Special disability leave still exists' — wrong, omitted in 2018.

title: Seamen's sick leave
statutory_text: 47. A seaman employed on a Government vessel may be granted sick leave for a period of six weeks on full pay, and for a further period of three months if he is disabled on duty; the concession is not available where the illness is due to malingering or self-indulgence.
summary: Seamen's sick leave: six weeks on full pay, extendable to three months if disabled on duty. Malingering or self-indulgence bars the leave.
hinglish: Seamen's sick leave: 6 hafte full pay par; duty par disabled ho to 3 mahine tak. Malingering ya self-indulgence ho to leave nahi.
conditions: Six weeks on full pay.
Three months where disabled on duty.
Government vessels only.
exceptions: Malingering or self-indulgence bars the leave.
authority: Head of Department
time_limit: 6 weeks; 3 months if disabled on duty
traps: 'Seamen's sick leave is three weeks' — wrong, six. 'Available on any vessel' — wrong, Government vessels only.

title: Special leave for an inquiry into sexual harassment
statutory_text: 48. A woman Government servant against whom an inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment is pending may be granted special leave for a period not exceeding 90 days during the pendency of the inquiry, on the recommendation of the Internal Committee or the Local Committee.
summary: Special leave of up to 90 days pending an inquiry into sexual harassment, on the recommendation of the Internal or Local Committee.
hinglish: Sexual harassment inquiry pending ho to aggrieved woman ko 90 din tak special leave — Internal ya Local Committee ki recommendation par.
conditions: Up to 90 days.
On the recommendation of the Internal or Local Committee.
During the pendency of the inquiry.
exceptions: The rule number here was substituted; the instrument is DoPT No. 13026/2/2016-Estt.(L), 15.03.2017.
authority: Ministry/Department (on the Committee's recommendation)
time_limit: 90 days
traps: 'Leave is 60 days' — wrong, 90. 'The servant must apply through Form 1' — the recommendation of the Committee is the trigger.

title: Departmental leave
statutory_text:
49. (1) Departmental leave may be granted to (a) Class III (other than Division I staff and clerks) and Class IV employees of the Survey of India with field or recess duties, and (b) seasonal staff of the Posts & Telegraphs Department.
(2) It may be granted only where the services of the servant are temporarily not required.
(6)(a) Leave salary is 25% of earned leave leave salary plus dearness allowance only.
(7) It does not count as duty and is not debited to the leave account.
(9) It may be combined with any other leave due.
summary: Departmental leave is confined to Survey of India field/recess staff and P&T seasonal staff. It runs only while the services are temporarily not required, pays 25% of EL leave salary plus DA, is not debited to the account, and may run up to 18 months in the recess.
hinglish: Departmental leave sirf Survey of India ke field/recess staff aur P&T seasonal staff ko. Jab services temporarily nahi chahiye tab milti hai. Salary = EL leave salary ka 25% + DA. Leave account se debit nahi, duty bhi nahi, aur 18 mahine tak recess mein.
conditions: Eligible: Survey of India Class III (except Division I staff and clerks) and Class IV with field/recess duties; P&T seasonal staff.
Only where the services are temporarily not required.
Leave salary: 25% of EL leave salary plus DA.
Not debited to the leave account; does not count as duty.
May be combined with any other leave due.
exceptions: Maximum in the recess: up to 18 months.
authority: Head of Party / Head of Office
time_limit: Up to 18 months in the recess
cross_refs: Rule 29(3) (20 days HPL after 12 months of actual duty); Rule 42
traps: 'Departmental leave pays full salary' — wrong, 25% plus DA. 'Open to all departments' — wrong. 'It counts as duty' — wrong.

title: Conditions for grant of study leave
statutory_text: 50. (1) Study leave may be granted to a Government servant with a definite sphere of duties who (i) has satisfactorily completed the period of probation and rendered not less than five years' regular continuous service including probation; (ii) is not due to reach the age of superannuation within three years (five years for a CHS officer granted 36 months' study leave) from the date of expected return; and (iii) executes a bond to serve Government for three years (five years for a CHS officer with 36 months' study leave) after expiry of the leave.
summary: Study leave needs a definite sphere of duties, five years' regular continuous service including probation, a return date at least three years before superannuation, and a bond of three years' service (five for CHS officers on the 36-month route).
hinglish: Study leave ke liye: definite sphere of duties, 5 saal regular continuous service (probation included), superannuation se 3 saal pehle wapsi, aur 3 saal ka bond (CHS officer ke 36-month route mein 5 saal).
conditions: Five years' regular continuous service including probation.
Not due to superannuate within three years (five for the CHS 36-month case) of the expected return.
Bond to serve three years (five for the CHS 36-month case).
exceptions: The service requirement is regular continuous service — probation must have been completed satisfactorily.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG (First Schedule — study leave)
time_limit: Five years' service; bond 3 years (5 for CHS)
traps: 'Three years' service is enough' — wrong, five. 'Two-year bond' — wrong, three (five for CHS). 'Any authority can sanction study leave' — wrong, only Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG.

title: Maximum study leave
statutory_text:
51. (1) The maximum amount of study leave admissible under these rules shall be twenty-four months in the entire service, ordinarily not more than twelve months at a time; for a CHS officer it is thirty-six months.
(2) This is inclusive of similar leave under any other rules.
summary: Study leave: 24 months in the entire service, ordinarily 12 months at a time; 36 months for CHS officers. The ceiling is inclusive of similar leave under any other rules.
hinglish: Study leave maximum 24 mahine poore service mein, aam taur par ek baar 12 mahine; CHS officer ke liye 36 mahine. Doosre rules ke under li gayi similar leave bhi ismein count hoti hai.
conditions: 24 months in the entire service.
Ordinarily not more than 12 months at a time.
CHS officers: 36 months.
Inclusive of similar leave under any other rules.
exceptions: The ceiling is for the entire service, not per post.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG
time_limit: 24 months (36 CHS); 12 months at a time
traps: '36 months for everyone' — wrong, only CHS. 'Unlimited extensions' — wrong, 24 or 36 in the entire service.

title: Application for study leave
statutory_text:
52. (1) A Government servant applying for study leave shall apply through the proper channel, and the course or courses of study contemplated and any examination he proposes to undergo shall be clearly specified in the application.
(2) Where full details cannot be given, or where a change is made after leaving India, particulars shall be submitted as soon as possible to the Head of the Mission or the authority competent to grant leave, and the course shall not be commenced at Government risk until approval is received.
summary: Study leave is applied for through the proper channel, with the course and the examinations clearly specified. Late details go to the Head of Mission or the sanctioning authority.
hinglish: Study leave proper channel se apply hoti hai, aur course + examinations clearly likhne padte hain. Bahar jaakar change ho to Head of Mission ya sanctioning authority ko batao — approval se pehle course Government risk par shuru nahi hota.
conditions: Application through the proper channel.
Course and examinations to be specified.
Changes reported to the Head of Mission or the sanctioning authority.
exceptions: Commencing the course before approval is at the servant's own risk.
authority: Head of Department / Ministry / Administrator / CAG
time_limit: Before the leave is to commence
traps: 'Study leave may be applied for directly to the sanctioning authority' — wrong, proper channel is mandatory.

title: Sanction of study leave and bond
statutory_text:
53. (1) A report regarding the admissibility of the study leave shall be obtained from the Audit Officer, including any study leave already availed of.
(2) Where the servant is borne on one department and serving in another, the concurrence of the parent department is required.
(3) Where study leave is granted for studies abroad, the Head of the Mission is informed.
(4)(a) A Government servant in permanent employ shall execute a bond in Form 7, or Form 8 for an extension, before the leave or extension commences.
(b) A servant not in permanent employ shall execute a bond in Form 9, or Form 10 for an extension.
(c) The sanctioning authority shall send the Audit Officer a certificate that the bond has been executed.
(5) On completion of the course, certificates of examinations passed and special courses, with commencement and termination dates, shall be submitted.
summary: Sanction of study leave needs the Audit Officer's admissibility report, the parent department's concurrence where the servant is on loan, and a bond: Form 7/8 for permanent staff, Form 9/10 for non-permanent staff, executed before the leave begins, with a certificate of execution to the Audit Officer.
hinglish: Study leave sanction: pehle Audit Officer ki admissibility report, loan case mein parent department ki concurrence, aur bond — permanent ke liye Form 7/8, non-permanent ke liye Form 9/10 — leave shuru hone se pehle. Bond execute hone ka certificate Audit Officer ko jaata hai.
conditions: Audit Officer's admissibility report.
Parent department's concurrence for a servant serving on loan.
Form 7/Form 8 bond: permanent staff.
Form 9/Form 10 bond: non-permanent staff.
Certificate of bond execution sent to the Audit Officer.
exceptions: The bond must be executed before the leave or extension commences.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG
time_limit: Bond before commencement; certificate to the Audit Officer
traps: Swapping Form 7/8 with Form 9/10 between permanent and non-permanent staff.

title: Accounting and combination of study leave
statutory_text:
54. (1) Study leave shall not be debited against the leave account.
(2) Study leave may be combined with other kinds of leave, but the grant of study leave in combination with leave other than extraordinary leave shall not involve a total absence of more than twenty-eight months generally and thirty-six months for courses leading to a Ph.D. degree from the regular duties.
Explanation — The limit of twenty-eight months or thirty-six months includes the period of vacation.
(3) A servant granted study leave in combination with other leave may undertake a course during the other leave and draw study allowance, but the period coinciding with the course shall not count as study leave.
summary: Study leave is not debited against the leave account. Combined absence is capped at 28 months generally and 36 months for a Ph.D. course, and the cap includes vacations.
hinglish: Study leave leave account se debit nahi hoti. Combination mein total absence 28 mahine (aam) aur Ph.D. ke liye 36 mahine — vacation bhi ismein count hota hai.
conditions: Not debited against the leave account.
Total absence in combination: 28 months; 36 months for Ph.D.
The limit includes the period of vacation.
exceptions: Study leave combined only with EOL is outside the 28/36-month cap.
authority: Audit Officer / sanctioning authority
time_limit: 28 months (36 for Ph.D.) total absence
forms: Form 2 (no debit entry for study leave)
traps: '28 months excludes vacation' — wrong. 'Study leave is debited like EL' — wrong. 'PhD limit 48 months' — wrong, 36.

title: Course falling short of the leave
statutory_text: 55. Where a course of study falls short of the period of study leave granted, the Government servant shall resume duty on the conclusion of the course, unless the previous sanction of the authority competent to grant leave treats the period of shortfall as ordinary leave.
summary: If the course ends early, the servant resumes duty unless previous sanction treats the shortfall as ordinary leave.
hinglish: Course jaldi khatam ho gaya to servant ko duty pe wapas aana hoga — jab tak sanctioning authority pehle se us shortfall ko ordinary leave treat na kare.
conditions: Resumption on conclusion of the course.
Shortfall treated as ordinary leave only with previous sanction.
exceptions: Previous sanction is mandatory for the shortfall conversion.
authority: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG
time_limit: At the conclusion of the course
traps: 'The servant may continue on study leave after the course ends' — wrong without previous sanction.

title: Leave salary during study leave
statutory_text: 56. (1)-(2) A Government servant on study leave shall draw leave salary equal to the pay last drawn plus dearness allowance and house rent allowance as admissible; the leave salary shall be adjusted against any scholarship, stipend or remuneration received, and shall in no case fall below the half pay leave salary admissible to him.
summary: Study leave salary is the pay last drawn plus DA and HRA as admissible. Scholarships and stipends are adjusted against it, and it never falls below the HPL salary.
hinglish: Study leave par pay last drawn + DA + HRA milti hai. Scholarship/stipend adjust hoti hai, lekin leave salary HPL salary se neeche nahi jaati.
conditions: Pay last drawn plus DA and HRA.
Scholarship or stipend adjusted.
Never below the HPL salary.
exceptions: Only DA, HRA and the study allowance are payable in addition — Rule 60(2).
authority: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
time_limit: Monthly during study leave
traps: 'Study leave is unpaid' — wrong. 'Allowances continue in full' — wrong, Rule 60(2) limits them.

title: Conditions for study allowance
statutory_text:
57. (1) A study allowance shall be granted to a Government servant who has been granted study leave for studies outside India, for the period spent in prosecuting a definite course of study at a recognised institution or in a definite tour of inspection, and for the period covered by any examination at the end of the course.
(2) Where the servant receives a scholarship, stipend or part-time remuneration, no study allowance is admissible if the net amount exceeds the study allowance otherwise admissible; if it is less, the difference may be granted.
(3) No study allowance for a period during which the servant interrupts the course for his own convenience; up to 14 days at a time may be allowed for sickness.
(5) Study allowance is allowed for the entire vacation during the course, and for a maximum of 14 days for vacation at the end.
(6) The period for which study allowance may be granted shall not exceed 24 months in all.
summary: Study allowance is for study outside India only. Interruptions for convenience earn nothing; up to 14 days at a time for sickness. Vacation during the course is covered, but end-of-course vacation only up to 14 days. The outer limit is 24 months.
hinglish: Study allowance sirf bahar desh ki study par. Apni convenience se course rok diya → allowance nahi; bimari par ek baar mein 14 din tak. Course ke dauran vacation poori count hoti hai, course ke end ki vacation sirf 14 din. Outer limit 24 mahine.
conditions: Study allowance only for studies outside India.
Definite course or tour of inspection; examination periods at the end of the course.
Sickness interruption: up to 14 days at a time.
Vacation during the course fully covered; end-of-course vacation up to 14 days.
Outer limit: 24 months.
exceptions: No study allowance for studies in India.
Scholarship or stipend reduces the allowance to the difference.
authority: Ministry/Department / Administrator / CAG
time_limit: 24 months in all; 14 days for sickness interruptions
traps: 'Study allowance is payable for study in India' — wrong. 'Interruptions are fully paid' — wrong. 'End-of-course vacation is unlimited' — wrong, 14 days.

title: Rates of study allowance — OMITTED
statutory_text: 58. [Omitted]
summary: Rule 58 is omitted. The old sterling per-diem table (£1.00 Australia to £2.75 USA) is historical, not law. Study allowance is now governed by Rule 57 only.
hinglish: Rule 58 omit ho chuka hai. Purani sterling per-diem table (Australia £1.00 se USA £2.75) sirf history hai — aaj study allowance Rule 57 se chalti hai.
conditions: Printed as 'Omitted' in the DoPT compilations updated 19.09.2022, 18.10.2023 and 24.09.2024.
exceptions: Do not quote sterling rates as current law.
time_limit: Omitted
traps: Quoting the sterling per-diem table as if it were current law.

title: Payment of study allowance — OMITTED
statutory_text: 59. [Omitted]
summary: Rule 59 is omitted. Certificate, monthly provisional payment and diary requirements no longer sit in the rules.
hinglish: Rule 59 omit hai. Certificate, monthly provisional payment aur diary wali requirements ab rules mein nahi hain.
conditions: Printed as 'Omitted' in the current DoPT compilations.
exceptions: Do not cite the old payment procedure as statutory.
time_limit: Omitted
traps: Treating the old monthly-certificate procedure as still statutory.

title: Allowances in addition to study allowance
statutory_text:
60. (1) House rent allowance may be paid during study leave for a period not exceeding 180 days, and thereafter only on production of a certificate as prescribed.
(2) Except for house rent allowance under sub-rule (1) and the dearness allowance and the study allowance, where admissible, no other allowance shall be paid in respect of the period of study leave.
summary: HRA for up to 180 days, then only against a certificate. Except HRA, DA and the study allowance, no other allowance is payable during study leave.
hinglish: Study leave mein HRA 180 din tak; uske baad certificate ke saath. HRA, DA aur study allowance ke alawa koi allowance nahi.
conditions: HRA up to 180 days.
After 180 days, HRA only against the prescribed certificate.
No allowance other than HRA, DA and the study allowance.
exceptions: The HRA limit is per period of study leave, not per year.
authority: Head of Office
time_limit: HRA 180 days
traps: 'All allowances continue during study leave' — wrong. 'HRA is payable for the whole period' — wrong, 180 days then certificate.

title: Travelling allowance during study leave
statutory_text: 61. A Government servant to whom study leave has been granted shall not ordinarily be paid travelling allowance, but the President may, in exceptional circumstances, sanction the payment of such allowance; for the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, the Comptroller and Auditor General may sanction TA in exceptional circumstances.
summary: TA is not ordinarily payable during study leave. The President may sanction it in exceptional circumstances; for the IA&AD, the C&AG may.
hinglish: Study leave par TA aam taur par nahi milta. President exceptional case mein sanction kar sakte hain; IA&AD ke liye C&AG.
conditions: TA is ordinarily not payable.
President may sanction in exceptional circumstances.
C&AG may sanction for the IA&AD.
exceptions: The IA&AD route is a specific statutory carve-out.
authority: President; C&AG for the IA&AD
time_limit: Exceptional circumstances
traps: 'TA is always payable for study leave' — wrong. 'C&AG may sanction for all departments' — wrong, only the IA&AD.

title: Cost of fees for study
statutory_text: 62. A Government servant to whom study leave has been granted shall ordinarily be required to meet the cost of fees paid for the study, but in exceptional cases the President may sanction the grant of such fees: provided that fees shall in no case be paid to a servant who is in receipt of a scholarship or stipend from any source, or who is permitted to retain remuneration for part-time employment.
summary: Fees are ordinarily the servant's own cost; the President may sanction them in exceptional cases, but never where a scholarship, stipend or part-time remuneration is held.
hinglish: Fees aam taur par servant khud bharega; President exceptional case mein sanction kar sakte hain — lekin scholarship/stipend ya part-time remuneration mil rahi ho to fees kabhi nahi.
conditions: Fees ordinarily borne by the servant.
President may sanction in exceptional cases.
exceptions: No fees where a scholarship or stipend is held, or part-time remuneration is retained.
authority: President
time_limit: Exceptional cases
traps: 'Fees are always paid by Government' — wrong. 'Fees are paid even with a scholarship' — wrong.

title: Refund on quitting service or failing the course
statutory_text:
63. (1) If a Government servant resigns or retires from service or otherwise quits service without returning to duty after study leave, or within three years after such return, or fails to complete the course and is unable to furnish the certificates required under Rule 53(5), he shall refund the actual amount of leave salary, study allowance, cost of fees, travelling and other expenses incurred by the Government of India, and the cost incurred by other agencies, together with interest at the rates in force on Government loans, before his resignation is accepted.
(2)(a) The study leave shall be converted into regular leave standing at his credit on the date the study leave commenced, and any balance that cannot be so converted shall be treated as extraordinary leave.
(3) The President may waive recovery in suitable cases.
summary: Quitting without return, or within three years of return, or failing the course, triggers refund of leave salary, study allowance, fees, TA and other expenses, plus interest. The leave is then re-converted into regular leave, with any balance treated as EOL. The President may waive.
hinglish: Wapsi ke bina quit kiya, ya wapsi ke 3 saal ke andar chala gaya, ya course fail → leave salary, study allowance, fees, TA sab interest ke saath refund. Study leave regular leave mein convert hoti hai, bacha hua EOL. President waiver kar sakte hain.
conditions: Refund applies on quitting without return or within three years of return.
Refund applies on failure to complete the course.
Interest at the rate in force on Government loans.
Conversion of study leave into regular leave under sub-rule (2).
exceptions: Exemptions: retirement on medical grounds after return, and absorption in a statutory or autonomous body in the public interest.
The President may waive recovery.
authority: President (waiver); sanctioning authority (recovery)
time_limit: Three years after return; interest from the date of demand
traps: 'The bond period is one year' — wrong, three (five for CHS). 'No interest is charged' — wrong.

title: Interpretation
statutory_text: 64. Where a doubt arises as to the interpretation of these rules, the matter shall be referred to the Government, whose decision shall be final.
summary: Doubts on interpretation go to the Government, and that decision is final.
hinglish: Rule ke matlab par doubt ho to Government ko refer karo — unka decision final hai.
conditions: Doubts are referred to the Government.
exceptions: The decision of the Government is final.
authority: Government (DoPT)
time_limit: As and when a doubt arises
traps: 'The Head of Office may settle the interpretation' — wrong, it goes to the Government.

title: Power to relax
statutory_text: 65. The President may, in exceptional cases, relax any of the provisions of these rules.
summary: The President may relax any provision in exceptional cases — a route for exceptions, not for ordinary administration.
hinglish: President exceptional cases mein kisi bhi rule ko relax kar sakte hain — yeh routine route nahi hai.
conditions: Relaxation is by the President.
exceptions: Only in exceptional cases.
authority: President
time_limit: Exceptional cases
traps: 'Any authority may relax the rules' — wrong, only the President. 'Relaxation is routine' — wrong.

title: Repeal and saving
statutory_text:
66. (1) The rules specified in the Second Schedule are repealed.
(2) Leave earned under the repealed rules is preserved, and anything done under the repealed rules shall be deemed to have been done under these rules.
summary: The rules in the Second Schedule are repealed, but leave already earned is saved and acts done under the old rules are deemed done under these rules.
hinglish: Second Schedule ke rules repeal ho gaye, lekin pehle se earned leave bachi rehti hai aur purane rules ke under kiye kaam naye rules ke under maane jaate hain — Rule 66(2).
conditions: Repeal of the rules in the Second Schedule.
exceptions: Leave already earned is preserved under Rule 66(2).
authority: President / Government
traps: 'The repeal wipes out leave already earned' — wrong, Rule 66(2) saves it.
